arm-01.note: buildRoute() geocodes stops through a TTL cache that calls Mapbox's geocoding API only when MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN is set (falls back to a deterministic local-street-offset); stop ORDER always uses its own nearest-neighbor, never Mapbox. Visual map is a hand-rolled SVG with an explicit "swap for Mapbox GL when a token exists" comment — no live Mapbox map.

arm-04.note: lib/routes/driver-access.ts and lib/shipping/margin.ts (the two files flagged as arm-04-unique) diff from arm-02 by only a trailing newline — functionally identical route-builder behavior.

arm-05.note: geocodeAddress() actually THROWS if MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN is missing outside TEST_MODE (stricter dependency on Mapbox than the clone cluster), but stop order is a naive lat-then-lng sort, not real nearest-neighbor/optimization, and there is no map visualization at all.

arm-06.note: Real Mapbox Optimized-Trips v1 API call for stop ORDERING (documented endpoint/params, waypoint_index re-sort) with a deterministic nearest-neighbor fallback on any failure/over-limit; UI surfaces which optimizer ran ("ordered by Mapbox" vs nearest-neighbor). Geocoding itself is deterministic-dev only (no Mapbox geocoding), and there's no visual map component.

arm-01.note: payment-reminders cron reminds every FINALIZED order with an open balance, deduped per order per calendar day; separate pickup-expiry cron stamps overdue ready pickups expired.

arm-05.note: sendPaymentReminders() is mis-scoped: it only reminds customers with a bulkDeliverySchedule whose order.paymentStatus === PENDING, missing general unpaid finalized orders entirely (a materially narrower cron than the name implies). Pickup expiry (expirePickupPackages) is a separate, correct sweep.

arm-06.note: sweepPaymentReminders() with a configurable cadence (first reminder after initialAfterDays, then every intervalDays via lastPaymentReminderAt) plus a CronRun audit row per run; sweepPickupExpiry() runs a readiness sync before the expiry pass — most sophisticated cadence of the six.

arm-01.note: planParcels(): real first-fit-decreasing multi-box bin packing (items sorted by volume, boxes tried smallest-first, 85% usable-volume ratio), with an oversized-item fallback that ships as its own dimensions rather than failing.

arm-05.note: parcelForPackage() sums ALL product volumes into one scalar and picks the smallest PackageType whose box volume >= that sum — no per-axis dimension check, no multi-box split, exactly one ShipmentBox per package always. Arm-05's own AGGREGATE-REVIEW-P8.md independently confirms: "'Bin packing' is a single-box volume-sum selection, not bin packing."

arm-06.note: planParcels(): best-fit-decreasing multi-parcel packing (smallest-fitting-open-parcel search, 85% fill ratio) — arguably a better placement heuristic than first-fit — but throws a hard DomainRuleError on an item that fits no configured box instead of gracefully shipping it as its own parcel.

arm-01.note: sweepNotificationOutbox(): conditional-UPDATE claim (pending/sending→claimed) so overlapping sweeps can't double-claim a row, stale-claim reclaim after 10 minutes, and a [1,5,15,60]-minute backoff schedule over MAX_ATTEMPTS=5.

arm-05.note: sweepEmailOutbox(): claim via updateMany on status=PENDING, stale PROCESSING reclaim after 10 minutes, fixed-delay retry (attemptCount * 60s) up to MAX_OUTBOX_ATTEMPTS=3, EmailLog row per outcome. Solid, marginally less backoff sophistication than the clone cluster.

arm-06.note: sweepOutbox() shares one claim/deliver module (lib/email/claim-deliver.ts) with the campaign send loop and test-sends, records a CronRun audit row per sweep, and deliberately excludes campaign-recipient and test-send kinds from auto-retry (an explicit, documented policy the other arms don't have).
